body: Does this issue only happen when you use function expressions inside a subquery, or does your `find('firstDue')` finder always have that same error? Does the error only happen when you use the computed field _and_ load additional associations with `contain()`?

I didn't use it without association. But this happens when I use function expressions inside a subquery. And if you look at the answer, when I used query string  `"id" => "TableName.id"`  it solves the problem for time being.
Ok, does it happen without the the finder being used as a subquery?
Yes. It does. Exactly the same error
@ndm2 what do you suggest as a fix?
Neat that the issue only shows up with an error handler registered.
I was able to reproduce this error locally, I'll get a fix together.

issue.title: Fix computed fields in contained associations

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
When selecting computed fields in contained associations, an object to string error would be emitted. This caused queries to work incorrectly in both PHP5.x and PHP7 but in different ways. By doing a slightly slower check we can avoid string conversion errors.

Refs #9326
